builds.name: Reference: Mana burst
builds.goal: Reference for Veigar: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A scaling burst mage who earns AP through spell hits and takedowns while using a cage to restrict movement. The cage creates a landing window for delayed W and a missing-health finisher. Fix earned AP and target missing health for R. Defensive builds may leverage existing AP but cage landing still determines output; no infinite stacks to justify tankiness. AP and penetration support a short spell sequence; Luden supplies mana/proc pressure.
builds.summary: AP and penetration support a short spell sequence; Luden supplies mana/proc pressure.
testPlan: Kit question for Veigar: Fix earned AP and target missing health for R. Defensive builds may leverage existing AP but cage landing still determines output; no infinite stacks to justify tankiness.

Start with the early core (Luden, then Shadowflame) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: AP and penetration support a short spell sequence; Luden supplies mana/proc pressure. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Veigar unleashes a bolt of dark energy that deals magic damage to the first two enemies hit. Units killed by this bolt grant Veigar some ability power permanently. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Mana is wasted on resource-free champions; target health and proc readiness change burst.

Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Mana is wasted on resource-free champions; target health and proc readiness change burst.
Full cost 16,800 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Luden, then Shadowflame. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff, Zhonya's Hourglass are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

kitEvidence.formula:
Veigar unleashes a bolt of dark energy, dealing [80 / 120 / 160 / 200 / 240 + (0.5 / 0.55 / 0.6 / 0.65 / 0.7) × AP] magic damage to the first two enemies hit.

If Veigar kills an enemy with this Ability, he gains @Spell.VeigarPassive:dQKillStacks@ stack of Phenomenal Evil. Large minions and large monsters grant @Spell.VeigarPassive:dQKillStacksLarge@ stacks instead.

Veigar's Abilities grant him [1] stack of Phenomenal Evil when they strike enemy champions. Takedowns on champions grant an additional [5] stacks.

Each stack of Phenomenal Evil grants Veigar [1] Ability Power.
Veigar twists the edges of space, creating a cage that Stuns enemies that pass through for [1.5 / 1.75 / 2 / 2.25 / 2.5] seconds. The cage lasts for 3 seconds.

Veigar summons dark matter from the sky, dealing [85 / 140 / 195 / 250 / 305 + (0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 1 / 1.1) × AP] magic damage.

Every @Spell.VeigarPassive:PStacksPerDarkMatterCDR@ stacks of Phenomenal Evil reduce this Ability's Cooldown by @Spell.VeigarPassive:DarkMatterCDRIncrement*100@%.

Veigar blasts an enemy champion with primal magic to deal between [175 / 250 / 325 + (0.65 / 0.7 / 0.75) × AP] and [(175 / 250 / 325 + (0.65 / 0.7 / 0.75) × AP) × (2)] magic damage, increasing with the target's missing Health. Damage is maximized against enemies below 33% Health.

builds.name: Stack-fed attack mage
builds.summary: Test stack-fed attack mage against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test stack-fed attack mage against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Phenomenal Evil grants AP from actual spell hits and takedowns; Nashor and Lich Bane turn earned AP into independent attack magic damage during Event Horizon control. Terminus serves mixed ordinary attacks without claiming the cage itself deals damage or grants stacks.
testPlan: Required state: Record realistic AP stacks and trap an enemy who cannot immediately escape.
Compare three cage-window attacks with Q/W burst at equal earned stacks.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Tiny attack range and cage cooldown make the mage vulnerable.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Attacks and item procs do not automatically grant passive AP stacks, which require ability hits.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Lich Bane, Rabadon's Deathcap, Terminus, Banshee's Veil, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.
